ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Acetylcholine can serve as an excitatory neurotransmitter, and its synthesis and release are shown in the schematic diagram. Answer the question according to the figure: If enzyme D is inactivated for some reason, will the postsynaptic neuron show continuous inhibition or excitation?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows mitochondria and synaptic vesicles inside the presynaptic neuron; the synaptic vesicles are labeled “A-C” and release it into the synaptic cleft. There are receptors on the postsynaptic membrane, which can bind with “A-C”. Near the synaptic cleft, “enzyme D” is labeled, and the figure shows that enzyme D can decompose “A-C” into “A” and “C”. Then reason: The question stem states that acetylcholine is an excitatory neurotransmitter, and “A-C” in the figure represents acetylcholine. Under normal circumstances, enzyme D decomposes acetylcholine, thereby terminating its continuous stimulation of receptors on the postsynaptic membrane. If enzyme D is inactivated, acetylcholine cannot be decomposed in time, will continue to exist, and will continuously act on receptors on the postsynaptic membrane. Since acetylcholine is an excitatory transmitter, the postsynaptic neuron will show continuous excitation.
